caseStudy.title: Case Study
caseStudy.meta: Naitways · March to July 2026 · Sole developer
caseStudy.heading: A cloud platform for running virtual machines across several servers
caseStudy.intro: Naitways, a French hosting and network operator, needed an internal platform to create and operate KVM virtual machines across multiple physical hosts. I designed and built it end to end in four months: back end, web interface, infrastructure integration and documentation. About 40,000 lines across three codebases.

control.name: Control plane
control.detail: FastAPI. Owns accounts, API keys, shared storage, audit and billing, and routes every operation to the right host.
control.size: ~12,200 lines of Python · 27 API routers · 25 database migrations

agent.name: Host agent
agent.detail: FastAPI, one per physical server. Drives libvirt: disks, network interfaces and consoles.

web.name: Web interface
web.detail: Nuxt 4 and TypeScript, with VNC and serial consoles in the browser.

sse.title: Live state without polling
sse.text: The interface had to show machine state, IP addresses, alerts and audit entries as they changed. The control plane keeps a stream open to every host and fans events out to browsers by topic over Server-Sent Events. The trade-off: the event bus lives in one process, so each service runs as a single worker.

libvirt.title: A seven-second endpoint
libvirt.text: Some endpoints intermittently took around 7 seconds. The cause was a bulk libvirt statistics call that polled every QEMU process over a shared connection. I measured the cost of each statistics flag and replaced the call with a lighter per-machine query.

caseStudy.note: Internal product: the source code is not public.

projects.title: Projects
projects.Those Who Listen: Cooperative survival horror game where voice cloning becomes the enemy. Real-time voice cloning (<300ms latency, 100% local processing) lets creatures mimic your teammates. Built with OpenVoice and PyTorch.
projects.LoCode: Web-based code editor powered by Monaco Editor (VSCode's engine) with SSH remote development, split panels, integrated xterm.js terminal, and an Electron desktop app for cross-platform use.
projects.Safekeeping: Hand-drawn 2D tower-defense game for Android and the web, built in Unity. Place towers and walls, run supply belts back to your keep and hold off wave after wave of raiders, who adapt their path to what you build. Playable in the browser, with an online leaderboard.
projects.Fortunes of 1877: Open-world trading game in development at Hogeschool Rotterdam, built in Unity. You captain a balloon-powered ship between floating islands, buying goods where they're cheap and selling them where they're wanted, and every docking is done by hand.
projects.Copaintes: Website for Copaintes, a bar in the 10th arrondissement of Paris: the menu, upcoming events, table reservations and the story of the place. A fast static site with search-engine structured data.
projects.Portfolio: This website: a statically generated portfolio in English and French, with light and dark themes, an animated canvas ribbon and a background that scrolls at its own speed.
projects.Glados: Programming language built from scratch in Haskell — lexer, parser, type checker, and bytecode VM. Supports user-defined functions, lambdas, scoping, built-in I/O, and a REPL with colored output.
projects.R-Type: Multiplayer space shooter game engine in C++ using an Entity Component System architecture for efficient entity management, with networked gameplay and SFML 3.0 rendering.
projects.Zappy: Three-part networked simulation: a C server managing teams and resources on a virtual planet, a C++/Raylib 3D GUI for real-time visualization, and autonomous Python AI agents competing for survival.
projects.42sh: Feature-rich UNIX shell in C supporting pipes, redirections, logical operators (&&, {'||'}), alias system, arrow-key history navigation, cursor movement, and multiple built-in commands.
projects.Arcade: Modular game framework in C++ where games and display modules (NCurses, SDL, SFML) compile as shared libraries (.so) and load dynamically at runtime through a plugin interface.
projects.Raytracer: 3D ray tracing engine in C++ rendering realistic scenes with configurable primitives, multiple light sources, and scene descriptions parsed from config files using libconfig++.
projects.Cryptography: Complete encryption suite in Python implementing AES symmetric encryption, RSA asymmetric key pairs, and PGP workflows — with a CLI tool for encrypting, decrypting, and signing messages.
projects.Neural Network: Multilayer perceptron built from scratch in Python with NumPy, without any ML framework — forward propagation, backpropagation with chain-rule gradients, sigmoid/Leaky ReLU activations, batch training, and JSON model persistence.
projects.JEB Incubator: Full-stack startup incubator platform with a Nuxt/Vue frontend, Deno backend API, MongoDB database, and Docker Compose deployment for streamlined local and production setup.
projects.Gomoku: AI player for Gomoku (5-in-a-row) in C++ with strategic board evaluation, game logging, and replay file generation. Implements the pbrain protocol for AI tournament compatibility.
projects.RPG: 2D RPG game engine in C with CSFML featuring sprite-based characters, enemies, collision detection, room transitions, and a custom world-building system with texture asset management.
projects.My Marvin: Jenkins CI/CD automation using Groovy Job DSL to define build pipelines, Dockerized Jenkins instance with plugin management, and YAML-based workflow orchestration.
projects.Vueling AI: Real-time voice translation for aircraft enabling crew-passenger communication across up to 5 languages. Analyzes flight manifest data to prioritize onboard languages, with offline support and two modes: announcements and conversations.
projects.IREP ChatBot: Hackathon-built AI chatbot using Flask and a locally-hosted Ollama LLM for natural language understanding, with SQLite for conversation persistence and context-aware responses.
projects.Flame Your Mind: Exit 8-inspired game where you play a scientist trapped in a burning lunar base. Find the differences between scenes to escape through the floors. Built with Godot 4 and Unreal Engine 5.
projects.Event Horizon 5min: 3D spaceship fighter set near a black hole's event horizon. Siphon energy from the singularity while time accelerates — you have 5 minutes to charge your warp drive. Features juicy animations and a tomato Easter egg. Built with Godot 4.
projects.Lost In Space: Solo arcade survival game where you pilot a small spaceship drifting through space. Dodge randomly spawning asteroids at increasing speed and survive as long as possible. Score based on survival time. Built with Godot 4.
projects.Robbers & Cat: Open-world heist game where you steal paintings for a cat mafia. Drive around the city, burglarize locations in Phasmophobia-style gameplay, and escape before the police catches you. Built with Godot 4.

about.title: About
about.bio: I'm a fourth-year software engineering student at Epitech Paris, currently on exchange at Rotterdam University of Applied Sciences. Over three internships at Naitways, a French hosting and network operator, I went from writing Python automation tools to building a cloud platform alone, back end and front end. I also like systems and games: a UNIX shell in C, a programming language in Haskell, and several games made with Unity and Godot. I work in French, Spanish and English.
